findings: One admitted signed retinal firing now fans out through fixed body-internal anatomy into eye-horizontal and palm-horizontal paths; real key 26 starts leftward palm movement and real key 87 starts rightward palm movement.
Both 64-step runs enter the intended real key's horizontal span near sequence 10 without receiving key identity, coordinates, desired direction, distance, score, contact verdict, or evaluator state.
The predecessor threshold arm leaves both palm trajectories identical, so the retinal-to-palm projection is necessary for visual-reach initiation.
The foveal successor makes the centered surface visible but both runs later reach a horizontal body boundary, independently refuting the stronger closed-loop reach claim.
The accepted hand trajectory, learner-only diagnostic fingerprint, checkpoint replay, semantic firewall, formatting, compilation, clippy, and warm regression budget remain intact.
residual_uncertainty: This supports visual-reach initiation only; it does not support stable hand-target alignment, intended contact, clicking, typing, grasping, or transfer to another morphology.
A closed-loop reach still needs a physical relation between the seen surface and the hand; foveal target visibility alone is insufficient.
The result uses one workstation morphology and one opposite real-key pair, and remains research-only development evidence rather than frozen authority.
